verdict.rationale: Hightouch documents a first-party Identity Resolution feature. It links related customer records and identifiers into unified identities in the warehouse, explicitly across devices and channels, and produces a Golden Record whose canonical field values are chosen by survivorship rules. The evidence does not explicitly cover stitching anonymous activity to known users, and it never shows configurable matching or merge rules; survivorship rules only pick field values after records are linked. missing for 10: explicit anonymous-to-known stitching documentation, documented configurable match/merge rules, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, anonymous and known activity stitches into one customer profile across devices, with documented and configurable identity-resolution rules

citations.quote: Identity Resolution links related customer records into unified identities in your warehouse, so every downstream product works from one consistent view of each person or account.
Resolve identities across devices and channels so teams can build on a more complete customer record.
Golden Record — a one-row-per-identity table of canonical field values (selected by survivorship rules)
Identity Resolution unifies a person's identifiers into one resolved identity
